item.title: Iran recloses Strait of Hormuz, deepening jet fuel crisis
item.description: The war in Iran has pushed the global aviation industry to a breaking point, with jet fuel prices nearly doubling since the conflict began and airlines across Europe, Asia, and North America now canceling flights and grounding aircraft as supplies dwindle.

item.title: North Korea fires ballistic missile into East Sea
item.description:
North Korea launched at least one ballistic missile eastward on Sunday, South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff confirmed, in the latest in a rapid succession of weapons tests that have heightened tensions across the Korean Peninsula this year.

The JCS said it detected the missile launch and was analyzing details of the firing, including its range and flight characteristics. The AFP, citing Yonhap, reported that the South Korean military had tracked the missile heading toward the East Sea, also known as the Sea of Japan.

item.title: Iran calls free transit through Hormuz 'a fiction' as Europe plans naval mission
item.description: Iran pushed back forcefully against European calls to reopen the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday, even as dozens of countries gathered in Paris a day earlier to plan a multinational naval mission to restore free passage through one of the world's most critical shipping lanes.

item.title: French peacekeeper killed as Lebanon ceasefire frays
item.description: Israeli forces continued shelling and demolition operations across southern Lebanon on Saturday, less than two days after a US-brokered 10-day ceasefire took effect, raising doubts about the durability of the truce even as a French UN peacekeeper was killed in a separate attack attributed to Hezbollah.

item.title: Penn State develops 3D-printed brain sensors tailored to each patient
item.description: Researchers at Penn State have unveiled a method for 3D printing soft, stretchable brain electrodes customized to the unique folds of each patient's brain, a development that could reshape how neurological diseases are monitored and treated.

item.title: Iran regains 60% of missile launchers during ceasefire, US intelligence estimates
item.description: Seven weeks after the United States and Israel launched Operation Epic Fury against Iran, American intelligence and military officials now estimate that Tehran still holds roughly 60 percent of its pre-war missile launchers and about 40 percent of its long-range attack drone arsenal, according to a report by The New York Times published on Friday. The assessment underscores a widening gap between the Trump administration's claims of having devastated Iran's military and the reality on the ground.

item.title: U.S. backs $50M rare earth project in South Africa to cut China reliance
item.description: A U.S.-backed project in South Africa aims to extract rare earth minerals from massive industrial waste dunes, part of a broader push by Washington to loosen China's grip on the critical minerals supply chain.

item.title: Trump sends envoys to Pakistan for new Iran talks
item.description:
President Donald Trump announced Sunday that White House envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are heading to Islamabad for a second round of direct negotiations with Iran, with talks set to begin Tuesday, as the ceasefire between Washington and Tehran approaches its April 22 expiration.

In an interview with Fox News, Trump warned that if Tehran does not agree to a deal, the whole of Iran will be "blown up," specifically threatening to target bridges and power plants. He demanded that Iran reopen the Strait of Hormuz and surrender its highly enriched uranium stockpile.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV prays at Angola shrine tied to slave trade
item.description: Pope Leo XIV on Sunday led a rosary prayer at the Sanctuary of Mama Muxima, a revered Catholic shrine in Angola built by Portuguese colonizers in the late 16th century that served as a hub in the transatlantic slave trade. The visit marked one of the most symbolically charged moments of the American pope's 11-day tour of Africa.

item.title: Trump reverses course, confirms Vance will lead Iran talks in Pakistan
item.description: In a confusing sequence of announcements on Sunday, President Donald Trump initially told ABC News that Vice President JD Vance would not travel to Pakistan for a second round of negotiations with Iran, only for the White House to later confirm that Vance would in fact lead the delegation. The back-and-forth unfolded as the administration scrambled to arrange talks ahead of a fragile ceasefire set to expire on Wednesday.

item.title: Iran refuses to send negotiators to Pakistan over US naval blockade
item.description: Iran has declared it will not send a negotiating delegation to Pakistan for a second round of peace talks with the United States as long as a US naval blockade of its ports remains in place, according to reports from Iran's semi-official Tasnim news agency on Sunday. The refusal throws into doubt plans announced by President Donald Trump, who said his representatives would arrive in Islamabad on Monday evening to resume negotiations.

item.title: Iran refuses to negotiate while US naval blockade remains in place
item.description: Iran has declared it will not send a negotiating delegation to Pakistan for a second round of peace talks with the United States as long as a US naval blockade of its ports remains in effect, according to Iran's semi-official Tasnim news agency on Sunday. The announcement throws into doubt a planned resumption of diplomacy just days before a fragile ceasefire is set to expire on April 22.

item.title: Trump says US seized Iranian ship as talks falter
item.description: President Donald Trump announced on Sunday that American forces had captured an Iranian-flagged cargo vessel near the Strait of Hormuz, escalating tensions just as Washington pushes to restart stalled peace negotiations with Tehran. Hours later, Iran rejected the proposed second round of talks, casting fresh doubt on the prospects for a diplomatic resolution before a fragile ceasefire expires on Wednesday.

item.title: Hamas signals readiness to hand over some weapons in Gaza
item.description: Two senior Hamas officials in Gaza have told The New York Times that the group is prepared to hand over thousands of automatic rifles and other weapons held by its police and internal security forces to a new Palestinian administrative committee, marking what could be the first concrete step toward disarmament — or a calculated attempt to deflect mounting international pressure.

item.title: Exit polls show Radev winning Bulgaria election by wide margin
item.description:
Former Bulgarian President Rumen Radev's Progressive Bulgaria coalition is on track to win Sunday's parliamentary election by a commanding margin, exit polls showed, raising hopes of ending years of political chaos in the Balkan nation but also stoking concern over a potential shift in the country's stance toward Russia and Ukraine.

Exit surveys by the Trend research group projected Radev's center-left coalition at roughly 39% of the vote, more than double the share of his closest rival, the center-right GERB party led by longtime Prime Minister Boyko Borissov, which polled at about 15%. A separate Alpha Research exit poll broadly confirmed the result. Six parties are expected to clear the 4% threshold needed to enter the 240-seat National Assembly.

item.title: UAE asks U.S. for dollar swap line as Iran war strains economy
item.description:
The United Arab Emirates has quietly initiated discussions with the United States about a potential financial safety net as the war with Iran continues to strain its economy, according to a report by The Wall Street Journal on Saturday.

UAE Central Bank Governor Khaled Mohamed Balama raised the idea of a dollar currency-swap line with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Federal Reserve officials during meetings in Washington last week, where the Central Bank of the UAE was participating in the IMF and World Bank spring meetings. U.S. officials described the overture as precautionary rather than a formal request, with Emirati representatives stressing that they have so far managed to avoid the worst economic consequences of the conflict but may still need a backstop.

item.title: US-Iran talks set for Monday as ceasefire nears expiration
item.description: The fate of Iran's enriched uranium stockpile has emerged as the central obstacle in ongoing negotiations between Washington and Tehran, with President Donald Trump claiming Iran "has agreed to everything" even as Iranian officials flatly reject any transfer of nuclear material abroad. A new round of talks is expected in Islamabad on Tuesday, April 21, with a fragile ceasefire set to expire by midweek.

item.title: China tests microwave beam to recharge drones midair
item.description:
Chinese scientists have demonstrated a system that wirelessly transmits power from a ground vehicle to a drone in flight using microwave energy, a development that could one day allow unmanned aircraft to stay airborne indefinitely.

The research, published on March 25 in the peer-reviewed Chinese journal Aeronautical Science & Technology, was carried out by a team from Xidian University, an institution known for its military technology work, according to the South China Morning Post. The system uses a car-mounted microwave emitter to beam energy to an antenna array fitted to the drone's underside — and critically, it works while both the vehicle and the aircraft are moving.

item.title: Iran adviser warns of wider sea conflict as Hormuz tightens again
item.description: Ali Akbar Velayati, a senior advisor to Iran's Supreme Leader Seyyed Mojtaba Khamenei, declared on Sunday that the era of Western powers imposing security "from across the oceans" has ended, warning that "any mischief will trigger a chain reaction." The remarks, posted on X, came as Iran doubled down on restricting maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and signaled that the conflict could extend to other global shipping chokepoints, including the Bab al-Mandeb strait off Yemen's coast.

item.title: Israel building permanent military bases in Gaza, satellite images show
item.description: An investigation by Al Jazeera's Digital Investigations Unit, drawing on satellite imagery from Planet Labs and Sentinel Hub, has revealed that Israel is systematically building permanent military infrastructure across Gaza, even as civilian reconstruction efforts have stalled and aid organizations describe the Trump administration's ceasefire plan as a failure.
